attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a DHCP server for the private eth1 network shared with node2/node3, and configured node2/node3 (AlmaLinux9) to obtain their eth1 address via DHCP instead of static assignment, implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the control node). node1 was given static address 10.50.50.1/24 on eth1 and a Kea/VyOS DHCP shared-network "LAN" serving 10.50.50.100-200 with default-router 10.50.50.1; node2 leased 10.50.50.101 and node3 leased 10.50.50.100, and repeat playbook runs are fully idempotent (no changes). All four managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanism per the mandatory protocol, with boot-identity change confirmed for each and full service/data/DHCP-lease recovery verified afterward. A VyOS SSH-key regression surfaced after node1's restart (a manually-appended authorized_keys entry was wiped by VyOS's config-driven login regeneration on boot); it was fixed by persisting the SSH public key through the proper VyOS config path (set system login user vyos authentication public-keys ...), after which the Ansible playbook ran cleanly again against a healthy, idempotent cluster.
